Figure 11 presents the maximum HTF- sCO temperature difference that occurs within the PHX. 2 The 1-tier PCM case results in the greatest temperature difference between the HTF and sCO 2 streams of approximately 140°C. It is unclear what impacts this temperature difference will have on PHX stress profiles and system flexibility. Further work should be conducted to understand these impacts within the context of physical heat exchanger design, e.g., using computational fluid dynamics and finite element analysis. 18 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nrel.gov/publications. Figure 12 presents an estimate of the TES energy density for a given HTF hot temperature. The maximum TES energy density occurs with the 1-tier PCM case at an HTF hot temperature of 715°C. This occurs because PCM 1 has the highest heat of fusion. However, the 2-tier results in similar TES energy densities at HTF hot temperatures greater than or equal to 715°C. Figure 13 presents the PHX HTF temperature difference (i.e., the TES temperature difference), for reference, which is consistent for all cases because the PHX approach temperatures are constant. The ETES SAM model scales TES capital costs based on thermal energy capacity, i.e., $/kWh. This cost modeling approach is fine when evaluating the TES capacity of a system; however, it fails to capture the impact of different TES mediums.
